page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.24xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz across 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. Memory is configured with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), AVX-512 (vnni, bf16), and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers top-tier memory bandwidth, recording 7667.03 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 385.55 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads, alongside 156.56 GB/sec in write bandwidth. Multi-core compute performance is robust, posting a stress-ng score of 103498.55 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 652.59 GB/sec. In in-memory key-value benchmarks, it achieved 171.63 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, and reached 212.53 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware acceleration extensions such as AMX enable strong CPU-based inference, achieving 4485.29 tokens/sec for small model prompt processing and 318.29 tokens/sec for medium 7B models. However, the instance lacks integrated local NVMe storage and GPUs, requiring remote EBS volumes for persistent storage. Baseline networking is provisioned at 100 Gbps, catering to distributed data architectures.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8ib.24xlarge consolidates high-density DDR5 memory and extensive core counts into a single bare-metal-equivalent Nitro partition, minimizing resource fragmentation for heavy enterprise workloads. It is suited for in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, large-scale ETL pipelines, real-time analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inferencing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the AWS Nitro System. Providing 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 768.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The CPU architecture supports AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets alongside a large 480 MB L3 cache. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth of up to 7667.03 GB/sec cached and 385.55 GB/sec uncached, achieving 171.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 212.53 GB/sec static web serving throughput. It features 100 Gbps baseline networking but provides no local instance storage or GPUs. This profile is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases, real-time data streaming, distributed caching, and CPU-based vector inferencing.
